edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.XI (Saturus: the garden of roses)

source_text: Sed et Saturus benedictus hanc uisionem suam edidit, quam ipse conscripsit. Passi, inquit, eramus, et exiuimus de carne, et coepimus ferri a quattuor angelis in orientem, quorum manus nos non tangebant. Ibamus autem non supini sursum uersi, sed quasi mollem cliuum ascendentes. Et liberato primo mundo uidimus lucem immensam, et dixi Perpetuae (erat enim haec in latere meo): Hoc est quod nobis dominus promittebat: percepimus promissionem. Et dum gestamur ab ipsis quattuor angelis, factum est nobis spatium grande, quod tale fuit quasi uiridiarium, arbores habens rosae et omne genus flores. Altitudo arborum erat in modum cypressi, quarum folia cadebant sine cessatione. Ibi autem in uiridiario alii quattuor angeli fuerunt, clariores ceteris: qui ubi uiderunt nos honorem nobis dederunt, et dixerunt ceteris angelis: Ecce sunt, ecce sunt, cum admiratione. Et expauescentes quattuor illi angeli, qui gestabant nos, deposuerunt nos. Et pedibus nostris transiuimus stadium uia lata. Ibi inuenimus Iocundum et Saturninum et Artaxium, qui eadem persecutione uiui arserunt, et Quintum, qui et ipse martyr in carcere exierat; et quaerebamus de illis ubi essent ceteri. Dixerunt nobis angeli: Uenite primum intro et salutate dominum.
pass_a_gloss: Saturus also published his own vision which he wrote out himself: that they had suffered and left the flesh and began to be carried east by four angels whose hands did not touch them, going not turned face-up upward but as if climbing a gentle slope, and with the first world left behind they saw a huge light, and he said to Perpetua at his side that this was what the Lord was promising and they have received the promise, and while being carried a great open space appeared like a park with rose-trees and flowers of every kind, the trees tall like cypress with leaves falling unceasingly, and there four other angels brighter than the rest gave them honor and said in wonder to the other angels behold they are here, and the four carrying angels in awe set them down, and they crossed on foot a racecourse by a broad road, and there they found Jocundus and Saturninus and Artaxius burned alive in the same persecution and Quintus who had died a martyr in prison, and they asked about them where the rest were, and the angels told them to go in first and greet the Lord.
pass_b_english: Blessed Saturus also published his own vision, which he wrote out with his own hand. We had suffered, he says, and we had left the flesh, and we began to be borne eastward by four angels, whose hands did not touch us. We went not turned face-up toward heaven, but as though climbing a gentle slope. And when the first world had been left behind, we saw an immense light, and I said to Perpetua, for she was at my side: This is what the Lord was promising us; we have received the promise. And while we were being borne by those same four angels, a great open space came before us, like a garden park, holding rose-trees and flowers of every kind. The trees stood tall as cypresses, and their leaves kept falling without ceasing.

There in the garden were four other angels, brighter than the rest. When they saw us they gave us honor, and said with wonder to the other angels: Behold, they are here, behold, they are here. And the four angels who were bearing us, struck with awe, set us down. And on our own feet we crossed a racecourse by a broad road. There we found Jocundus and Saturninus and Artaxius, who in the same persecution had been burned alive, and Quintus, who himself had died a martyr in prison; and we kept asking them where the rest were. The angels said to us: Come inside first and greet the Lord.

choices.why: exeo with de plus ablative marks departure from a prior state, and caro here is the mortal body in a martyrdom context, not meat as food
supini describes posture lying on the back and sursum uersi gives direction, contrasting with the upward slope-climbing image that follows

choices.english: when the first world had been left behind
choices.why: ablative absolute with libero marks passing beyond one stage of the ascent, fitting the sequence from ascent to light to garden
